name: Judgement Window
description: The arbiter of timing: each note input is compared against the song position and graded perfect, good, or miss by tiered windows. It owns the window widths, the delta calculation, and the unhit-note miss — the note that scrolls past the receptor untouched is as much a judgement as a late press, and both must come from one place or combo counting forks. Deltas are corrected by utility.beat_clock's calibrated latency before grading, because a perfect press on a laggy headset is a perfect press; the correction lives in the clock, this component consumes it, and neither duplicates the other. It deliberately does not score: a tier is a fact, and what a perfect is worth — points, combo, health — belongs to economy.combo_multiplier and whoever else listens. Grading against time rather than frames is deliberate: frame-graded rhythm games change difficulty with the frame rate.

inputs.name: perfectWindowSeconds
inputs.description: Absolute delta for the top tier. 45 ms is the mainstream rhythm default — tight enough to mean something, loose enough to be humanly repeatable.

inputs.name: goodWindowSeconds
inputs.description: Absolute delta for the middle tier. The gap between perfect and good is the accuracy skill ceiling; the gap between good and miss is the game's forgiveness.

inputs.name: missWindowSeconds
inputs.description: Beyond this delta a press does not count at all. Capping the miss window prevents mashing early through dense sections from registering as late hits.

inputs.name: allowEarlyHits
inputs.description: Whether early presses grade symmetrically with late ones. Symmetric is standard; late-only grading suits games that punish anticipation.

outputs.name: lastDeltaSeconds
outputs.description: Signed, latency-corrected offset of the last press from its note. Published so practice UI can show 'early by 12 ms' instead of a bare tier.
